title: 1,8-Cineole alleviates Nrf2-mediated redox imbalance and mitochondrial dysfunction in diabetes mellitus by targeting Sirt1.
authors: Yang, Hong; Chen, Yong-Xin; Linghu, Ke-Gang; Ren, Peng-Yan; Yao, Yu-Ting; Jiang, Feng; Wu, Guo-Ping; Chen, Ting-Ting; Ji, Yun-Peng; Tao, Ling; Sun, Qian-Yun; Li, Yue; Shen, Xiang-Chun
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究1,8-Cineole通过靶向Sirt1缓解糖尿病氧化应激，虽含分子对接但核心为小分子-蛋白互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is primarily attributed to impaired insulin secretion caused by beta cell dysfunction. 1,8-Cineole is a key bioactive compound in the essential oil extracted from Fructus Alpiniae Zerumbet, which possesses anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. Nevertheless, it remains elusive about the protective effect and precise mechanisms of 1,8-Cineole against the beta cell deterioration in T2DM. PURPOSE: To investigate the effect of 1,8-Cineole on beta cell dysfunction in T2DM and the potential mechanism of its action. METHODS: A mouse model of T2DM and a beta cell model of high glucose induction were generated to analyze the pharmacological properties of 1,8-Cineole. Proteomic and network pharmacological analyses were conducted to identify the crucial pathways involved in T2DM. Resveratrol [a Sirtuin1 (Sirt1) agonist] and Sirt1 knockdown were used to ascertain the mechanism of 1,8-Cineole in T2DM. The binding affinity of 1,8-Cineole to Sirt1 was assessed with molecular docking, surface plasmon resonance, immunoprecipitation assay, and cellular thermal shift assay. RESULTS: Firstly, dysregulated crucial pathways in T2DM were screened out, including redox imbalance and mitochondrial dysfunction. Subsequently, 1,8-Cineole was found to activate Sirt1 and nuclear factor E2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) to repress oxidative stress in both T2DM mice and high glucose-induced beta cells, thereby relieving mitochondrial dysfunction and apoptosis. Furthermore, 1,8-Cineole specifically targeted Sirt1 and favored the direct interaction between Sirt1 and Nrf2, ultimately restoring beta cell function. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings provide the first evidence that 1,8-Cineole directly binds to Sirt1 and enhances its stability, therefore rectifying impaired oxidative homeostasis, and then suppressing mitochondrial dysfunction and apoptosis in T2DM, indicating that 1,8-Cineole may be a potential candidate drug for T2DM treatment.
abstract_zh: 背景：2型糖尿病（T2DM）主要归因于β细胞功能障碍导致的胰岛素分泌受损。1,8-桉叶素是从益智仁（Fructus Alpiniae Zerumbet）精油中提取的关键生物活性化合物，具有抗炎和抗氧化特性。然而，1,8-桉叶素对T2DM中β细胞退化的保护作用及其精确机制仍不明确。目的：研究1,8-桉叶素对T2DM中β细胞功能障碍的影响及其潜在作用机制。方法：建立T2DM小鼠模型和高糖诱导的β细胞模型，以分析1,8-桉叶素的药理特性。采用蛋白质组学和网络药理学分析，以识别T2DM中涉及的关键通路。使用白藜芦醇（一种Sirtuin1（Sirt1）激动剂）和Sirt1敲低，以确定1,8-桉叶素在T2DM中的作用机制。通过分子对接、表面等离子体共振、免疫沉淀实验和细胞热位移实验评估1,8-桉叶素与Sirt1的结合亲和力。结果：首先，筛选出T2DM中失调的关键通路，包括氧化还原失衡和线粒体功能障碍。随后，发现1,8-桉叶素激活Sirt1和核因子E2相关因子2（Nrf2），以抑制T2DM小鼠和高糖诱导的β细胞中的氧化应激，从而缓解线粒体功能障碍和凋亡。此外，1,8-桉叶素特异性靶向Sirt1，并促进Sirt1与Nrf2之间的直接相互作用，最终恢复β细胞功能。结论：我们的研究结果首次证明，1,8-桉叶素直接结合Sirt1并增强其稳定性，从而纠正受损的氧化稳态，进而抑制T2DM中的线粒体功能障碍和凋亡，表明1,8-桉叶素可能是T2DM治疗的潜在候选药物。
